question: In Unhais da Serra, in the Serra da Estrela natural park, more than 20 healthy plane trees – most of which over a hundred years old – have been inexplicably felled or pruned. The operation, classified as an ‘environmental upgrade’ by Covilhã Municipal Council, has significant environmental consequences and was carried out without any public notification, justification or explanation.

Concerns have also been raised about the trees that have escaped felling. Information at the site explains that the felling is designed to ‘(re)introduce trees to green spaces and create shade in built-up areas’ and receives EU funding. I would like to know what EU funds were used specifically for this process and to what extent the consequences are in line with the objectives of those programmes and measures?
answer: This project of requalification of ‘Avenida das Termas’ is financed by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) through the Competitiveness and Internationalisation programme for Portugal (COMPETE 2020) under Priority Axis VII: Fostering crisis repair in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and its social consequences and preparing a green, digital and resilient recovery of the economy.

The intervention was categorised, among others, as a measure of prevention and management of risks linked to climate change. The scope of the project was wider than the tree felling mentioned by the Honourable Member. It included interventions for environment requalification but also for the safety and protection of both residents and tourists.
The measures under the project also include planting of 44 trees (plum trees, orange trees and olive trees), the construction of a lawn of 1200m2 and an irrigation system.

Based on the information provided by the Portuguese authorities, the beneficiary considered that the felling of 25 trees and pruning of 14 others was urgent to ensure safety of people and goods which fall under the scope of prevention and management of risks. The initial overall budget of the project was EUR 70 300, financed 100% by the EU and actual expenditure incurred was EUR 57 138.16.
